links.outcome: Escalation insufficiency rate in clinician-evaluated responses from safety-gated RAG system
links.effect: Escalation insufficiency (0.6% of all dialogs) rarely occurred; 91.6% (437/477) of responses clinically appropriate.
links.quote: Clinically inappropriate responses (8.4%) were mainly attributable to information insufficiency; not FBT concordant (1.8% of FBT-related responses) and escalation insufficiency (0.6% of all dialogs) rarely occurred.

links.outcome: Clinician review of AI responses for clinical appropriateness and safety
links.effect: Six clinicians rated 91.6% (437/477) of responses clinically appropriate; 8.4% inappropriate, mainly information insufficiency.
links.quote: The clinically appropriate response rate was 91.6% (437/477), including 92.3% for FBT-related questions, 88.0% for general knowledge, 93.7% for psychological distress, and 100.0% for other questions.

unlisted_practices: Sentiment-triggered empowerment messages to maintain caregiver confidence
Guardrails prohibiting unsolicited numerical goals or direct hospitalization recommendations

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an AI agent with integrated safety guardrails and RAG for family support in anorexia nervosa treatment using clinician-authored simulated queries, but it evaluates the overall novel system without an ablation or comparative test of specific deployment practices.
